source.title: The Loss Does Not See the Basis, but Adam Does

record.tranche_reason: Tests optimizer-related generalization on hyperspectral matrix-completion benchmarks, a new setting relative to V4's image-classification and language benchmarks.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own matched-training-loss held-out RMSE comparisons on two hyperspectral datasets. Cited optimizer comparisons are not recorded as rows. The attention-twin results measure basis-dependent divergence, not the generalization behavior named by the versions.
record.test_reason: The study tests V4's optimizer-dependent held-out performance in a new setting: overparameterized matrix completion. GD and Adam reach matched training losses, but Adam has higher held-out RMSE. This extends the comparison beyond the classification and language benchmarks named in V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the hyperspectral result but understates the paper's central conclusion: internal gauge symmetry helps explain optimizer-dependent interpolant selection in factored models, while spectral dynamics and computational budget also matter. GD beats Adam at matched training loss on both hyperspectral datasets, with smaller advantages at higher density and under held-out-informed learning-rate selection. Equivariance alone guarantees neither low-rank recovery nor better generalization.
record.recipe_differences: Compared with V4's image-classification and language-model optimizer comparisons, this study tests rank-48 factored matrix completion on hyperspectral data, matching training loss and reporting held-out RMSE.
record.method_sensitivity: The GD–Adam gap narrows as sampling density increases. Its reported magnitude depends on learning-rate selection: the train-only rule gives larger gains than choosing each method's rate by held-out error. Results are reported at matched loss thresholds.

fits_no_version.finding: Muon is worse than GD in all four hyperspectral conditions, worse than Adam on Indian Pines, and better than Adam on Pavia.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Spectral optimizer performance on matrix completion depends on the target spectrum and the optimizer's spectral schedule.

fits_no_version.finding: Adam's held-out RMSE rises from 0.0251 to 0.0268 as training loss falls and effective rank increases from 22 to 28.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Deeper fitting with Adam can worsen hyperspectral completion error while effective rank increases.

fits_no_version.finding: Gauge-equivalent transformer initializations diverge immediately under Adam, whereas equivariant optimizers remain at numerical precision at the first step.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adam's attention-head training dynamics depend on the internal factorization basis.

fits_no_version.finding: Synthetic sensing experiments compare planted-matrix recovery and effective rank across optimizers, learning rates, initialization scales, and spectral tails.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer geometry and spectral dynamics affect low-rank recovery from underdetermined measurements.

record.problems: The paper reports four random seeds for the hyperspectral comparisons. The size of the GD–Adam gap depends on the learning-rate selection criterion, and scalar-Adam's rate grid is described as undersampled. The study does not establish that its results transfer to the image-classification or language benchmarks named in V4.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying results omitted. The paper reports further optimizer recovery, rank, and gauge-drift results in §§5–10 and appendices; they do not measure the generalization behavior named by the listed versions, except the matched-loss GD–Adam test-error comparisons recorded here.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy.
Width-dependent test error beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.

The named classification and language benchmark comparisons; stochastic or momentum SGD comparisons at matched fit; broader hyperparameter tuning; decoupled weight decay; switching optimizers; and Adam's word-level language-model advantage.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects, training-set size dependence, and removal with weight decay under augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and comparisons with other generalization measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus randomly selected examples.

missing.what: Learning-rate sensitivity of the qualifying GD–Adam held-out comparison: Adam's tested rates yield RMSE/effective-rank pairs 0.0171/17, 0.0198/20, and 0.0260/27; selected GD yields approximately 0.0148/13. Selecting by held-out error reduces GD's advantage from approximately 43% to 13%, without reversing it.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for any version. A new task and untested tuning procedures do not themselves justify limits_scope. The reported tuning sensitivity changes the size of the GD–Adam gap while preserving its direction. The synthetic recovery and attention-divergence findings do not directly measure the held-out performance comparison named by V4.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and held-out accuracy on natural labels.
No width sweep or test-error comparison around the width needed for zero training error.
No convolutional versus fully connected image-classifier comparison.

Tests GD versus Adam on hyperspectral matrix completion, not the listed image-classification or language benchmarks; it does not compare the full range of adaptive methods or tuning protocols in the version.
No batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets.
No removal of memorized training examples.
